title: One Java Annotation Stops Cascading Microservice Failures
description:
When a downstream microservice starts failing, hammering it with retries just makes things worse. Spring's circuit breaker annotation from Resilience4j trips once failures cross a threshold, skipping the network entirely and routing straight to a fallback -- giving the failing service room to recover. This is one pattern from the microservices architecture lesson in the Java Mastery Path.

Source lesson:
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/java-mastery-path/level-4/02-microservices-architecture/

#Shorts

beats.narration: Picture a downstream service going down. Your app keeps calling it, again and again, burning threads while nothing comes back.
One annotation fixes this: circuit breaker. Wrap the risky call, and if it starts failing, Java reroutes it to a fallback method automatically.
Once half of the last twenty calls fail, the circuit trips open. Every call after that skips the network completely and goes straight to the fallback.

display.code:
resilience4j:
  circuitbreaker:
    instances:
      inventoryService:
        sliding-window-size: 20
        failure-rate-threshold: 50   # percent
        wait-duration-in-open-state: 10s

beats.narration: That's the whole point: stop hammering a service that's already struggling, and give it room to recover before you try again.
Full breakdown of gateways, sagas, and circuit breakers is in the microservices lesson, link below.
